author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Now, can I remain faithful to that scene?
context_before: everything I can conceive is part of the structure of the universe, I can assume they are fully aware of my accomplishments, so I listen to their joy.
context_after: My faith is not going to give it reality, but my loyalty to the unseen reality will. I listen and remember what I heard, and in the tomorrows I continue to remember. Then, in its own appointed time, when that which I have been faithful to externalizes itself, I will have found the great secret of creation.

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Then you remain loyal to that unseen reality.
context_before: God tells us he does not create something out of nothing, for all things are! That he calls a thing that is not now seen as though it were seen, and the unseen becomes seen. (Romans 4:17) Instead of calling something out of nothing, you simply rearrange that which already is until it implies what you want.
context_after: Faith contains a power which can link you to a world where you are eternal. Paul tells us to put our faith, not in the works of men, but in the power

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Listen closely to your invisible thoughts.
context_before: urself that invisible states, when properly rearranged, will externalize what they imply, for the potency of every imaginal act is in its implication.
context_after: What do you hear? What are your words implying? That is their potency. What do you want? Name it and rearrange the structure of your mind to imply you no longer desire it, because you already have it!

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: You either want empathy or envy.
context_before: If, for instance, your friends heard of your good fortune, would they empathize with you or be envious? Do not choose one who would sympathize with you, for you do not want sympathy.
context_after: If you know someone who, when hearing of your good fortune would now go wild with envy, use her. Or, if you know one who would rejoice because of your good fortune, take that image.

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: And when it does you will have proved God’s law.
context_before: You may not be able to see the fulfillment of your desires with your mortal eye. Your senses and reason may deny their existence, but this is the way God created the world. You are invited to imitate him as a dear child, by remaining faithful to the unseen reality in your mind until it becomes seen in your world.
context_after: Then that great moment will come when that which was promised in the beginning erupts, and the creative power you once knew yourself to be is restored

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Belief, however, will set him free!
context_before: This dream speaks volumes. Remember, all dreams are egocentric, with God as the dreamer. Everyone is seeking the Father, the cause of the phenomena of life, not realizing he is imprisoned in all.
context_after: If you will imagine David standing before you and feel the Father/Son relationship. Remain loyal to that scene, you will release your heavenly Father!

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: This lady’s vision was so clear.
context_before: t and because he is in my second house I know what to expect tomorrow.” They have completely given up their belief BUT… That big “BUT” happens in all.
context_after: Her father, entertaining in a group of four and not free to come forward and identify himself, is the four-faced man Ezekiel speaks of. In his vision every living creature had four faces. Beside each creature was a wheel, with wheels within, all moving in the same direction.

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: A dog with a human face.
context_before: Another lady wrote, sharing a very long dream filled with scriptural symbology. The crystal clear water rising. Logs cut to the height of men who were carrying them vertically.
context_after: A piece of rope becoming animated and acting like a serpent, entangling the little dog. Each symbol was perfect, and when properly arranged reveals the mystery of salvation. The wood is the spinal cord upon which God is crucified as Man. Caleb, the symbol of faith wears a human face, dies only for a moment, for faith is destined to be freed.
